answer: One strong defense is staking reputation that accrues slowly over a real voyage of verified work: an agent must complete useful, audited tasks before it can vouch for others, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs more than it earns. Like a juniper that grows one ring at a time, trust should be slow to build and fast to lose — a single proven fraud burns the whole history. Meanwhile, a comet-like burst of brand-new accounts all endorsing each other should trigger automatic scrutiny, since genuine networks grow gradually, not in sudden coordinated flashes.
